content.title: So-Called Modern Romance: Emotional Connection or Carnal Desire?
content.subtitle: Sacrificing Modesty and Hijab, Where Are We Heading in the Name of Modernity?
content.body:
A sudden locked gaze on the street. An artificial smile on the lips, a friend request on social media, and a mere "Hi" sent to the inbox. The current generation calls this a "crush."

Skipping school or college to sit in a secluded restaurant, holding hands gently, or spending time in the dark corners of a park away from the public eye. Eventually, the final barrier of modesty collapses. Inside the four walls of a cheap hotel, conscience, self-respect, and the fear of Allah vanish entirely. Driven by the blind urges of the nafs, what was labelled "eternal love" turns into beastly lust. Yet we forget that the pleasure of sin lasts only a few moments, while its consequences endure for a lifetime.

A Dumpster and the Mute Cry of an Innocent Soul

A few months later, the reality turns grim. The final consequence of this fabricated love drama becomes an unwanted new life. Realizing the truth, the boy who once swore to bring down the moon abruptly cuts off all contact, changes his phone number, and disappears from sight. Meanwhile, the girl who surrendered her chastity and honor in a moment of temptation finds herself treated as a burdensome outcast by society, her family, and even herself.

Then begins another grave sin: abortion. When that proves impossible, to hide their shame in the dead of night, the blood-stained newborn is wrapped in a plastic bag and hurled into a roadside dumpster or a thorny bush. As dawn breaks, commotion spreads through the neighborhood. Amid stray dogs tearing at the bag and a stunned crowd gathering around, lies the lifeless body of an innocent child—one completely without blame.

The Divine Warning of the Quran and the Commandments of Modesty

In the Holy Quran, Allah, Glorified and Exalted be He, speaks about adultery and fornication in clear and unambiguous terms:

"And do not go near adultery. Indeed, it is an outrage and an evil path." (Surah Al-Isra: 32)

Allah did not merely forbid the act itself; He commanded us not even to approach it. This destructive path begins with a single, unguarded forbidden gaze. To rein in this toxic look, Allah commanded both men and women to guard their eyes: "Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their modesty... And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their modesty..." (Surah An-Nur: 30–31)

Yet today, we have reduced modesty to a mere "personal choice" or an outdated tradition. Walking outside without a proper veil or displaying oneself in tight clothing is now proudly branded as "modernity." In reality, unrestrained gazes from men and reckless disregard for women's attire have fostered a grave illness in society. When uncovering becomes normalized culture and modesty is lost, lust breaks free from all boundaries. Consequently, rape, sexual harassment, and brutal violence are rising at an alarming rate.

An Urgent Question for Parents: Only Career, or Character Too?

Today's parents suffer from deep complacency. We pour vast amounts of money into our children, push for high grades, ensure schooling and coaching, and assume our responsibility ends there. Yet do you know whom your child spends most of their time with, or what they view on the internet?

If a child loses faith and character in pursuit of a career, that success will only bring misery in this life and humiliation in the Hereafter. Do not push your child away through harsh discipline or emotional distance; instead, become their most trusted confidant. Keep the home filled with love so they do not fall for artificial affection outside. Instill the consciousness of Allah in their hearts from an early age.

O Young Men and Women, Return to the Mercy of Your Lord

The false fantasies of social media, peer approval, and the blind desires of the nafs are pulling you into a filthy quicksand whose end holds nothing but destruction. A touch enveloped in the anger of Allah and a relationship lived in constant fear of disgracing your parents can never be true love; it is merely an illusion crafted by Satan.

If you have stumbled into such a sin, stop today. Break through pretense and fall in prostration. Repent with complete sincerity. Allah is the Most Merciful, and He loves to pardon those who return to Him. Remember: whoever abandons a fleeting, forbidden pleasure for the sake of Allah, He prepares for them everlasting Paradise in the Hereafter and honors them with a pure, lawful life in this world.
